definitions.explanation: The portion of a passage marked with an underline. Standard wording in exam questions and textbook exercises, which routinely ask about {下線部|かせんぶ}.

examples.japanese: {下線部|かせんぶ}を{訳|やく}しなさい。
{下線部|かせんぶ}の{意味|いみ}を{説明|せつめい}してください。
examples.english: Please explain the meaning of the underlined part.

examples.japanese: {下線部|かせんぶ}が{何|なに}を{指|さ}しているか、{本文|ほんぶん}の{中|なか}から{探|さが}して{答|こた}えなさい。
examples.english: Find in the passage what the underlined part refers to, and answer accordingly.

notes:
From {下線|かせん} (underline) + {部|ぶ} (part). When several passages are underlined they are numbered: {下線部|かせんぶ}(1), {下線部|かせんぶ}(2).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下線部|かせんぶ}を{訳|やく}す: to translate the underlined part
- {下線部|かせんぶ}について{答|こた}える: to answer about the underlined part
- {下線|かせん}を{引|ひ}く: to underline

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}: the marked part — the same idea in Japanese-language exams, where the line runs beside vertical text
- {空欄|くうらん}: blank — the gap to be filled in a fill-in-the-blank question
